items.question: How many engines does the basic AW139 installation have and what is their general type?
options: Two turboshaft engines with dual-channel FADEC each.
Three piston engines driving a common gearbox.
Two turbofan engines with manual fuel control.
items.explanation: The AW139 is a twin-engine helicopter with two FADEC-controlled turboshaft engines driving a common main gearbox.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Powerplant – General

items.question: What is the primary function of the FADEC on each AW139 engine?
options: Automatically schedule fuel to maintain selected rotor/engine parameters within limits.
items.explanation: The FADEC automatically schedules fuel and manages engine operation to keep rotor and engine parameters within their prescribed limits.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Powerplant – FADEC

items.question: In normal operation, where do the AW139 engine-driven main fuel pumps take their fuel supply from?
options: From a single header tank independent of the main tanks.
Directly from each engine's associated main tank via boost pumps and selector valves.
From the auxiliary power unit (APU) tank only.
items.explanation: Each engine-driven pump normally draws fuel from its associated main tank through the aircraft fuel supply system.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fuel System – Description

items.question: What is the purpose of the fuel cross-feed capability in the AW139 fuel system?
options: To allow either engine to be supplied from the opposite tank in case of low fuel or pump failure.
To transfer fuel only during refuelling.
To feed the APU when both engines are shut down.
items.explanation: Cross-feed allows one engine to be supplied from the opposite side tank in abnormal or emergency conditions, increasing flexibility and redundancy.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fuel System – Crossfeed

items.question: Where are the main fuel quantity indications presented to the crew in the AW139?
options: On mechanical gauges in the cabin floor.
On the fuel page of the MFD/EDCU displays.
items.explanation: Fuel quantity is normally indicated on the dedicated fuel page on the EDCU/MFD displays.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fuel System – Indications

items.question: What is one of the purposes of the AW139 fuel system ventilation (vent) lines?
options: To provide bleed air to the cabin heating system.
To maintain tank pressure close to ambient and allow for fuel expansion and contraction.
To transfer fuel between the main and auxiliary tanks automatically.
To provide lubrication oil return from the engines.
items.explanation: Ventilation lines keep tank pressure close to ambient and accommodate volume changes due to temperature and fuel movement.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fuel System – Ventilation

items.question: What is the basic function of the main gearbox (MGB) on the AW139?
options: Convert high-speed, low-torque engine output to low-speed, high-torque drive for the main and tail rotors.
items.explanation: The MGB reduces engine RPM and transmits torque to the main and tail rotors as low-speed, high-torque drive.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission System – General

items.question: Which system primarily lubricates and cools the AW139 main gearbox?
options: A self-contained oil system with pump, cooler and filters.
Only natural splash lubrication without a pump.
items.explanation: The MGB uses a dedicated oil system with pump, cooler and filters to lubricate and cool the gears and bearings.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission – Lubrication

items.question: What is the function of chip detectors installed in the MGB and TRGB on the AW139?
options: Detect metal particles in the oil, indicating possible gear or bearing damage.
items.explanation: Chip detectors sense metallic particles in gearbox oil, giving early warning of internal damage.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission – Chip Detectors

items.question: Which of the following best describes the AW139 hydraulic system architecture?
options: A single hydraulic system supplying all consumers.
Two independent hydraulic systems with interconnections supplying flight controls and other users.
Three completely isolated hydraulic systems with no interconnection.
No hydraulic system; controls are entirely manual.
items.explanation: The AW139 has two main hydraulic systems with some interconnections, supplying primary flight controls and other users.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Hydraulic System – General

items.question: Which primary flight controls on the AW139 are powered by the hydraulic systems?
options: Cyclic, collective and tail rotor controls.
items.explanation: Both hydraulic systems supply the servos for cyclic, collective and tail rotor controls.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Hydraulic System – Description

items.question: What is the purpose of the Electric Hydraulic Pump System (EHPS) on the AW139?
options: Provide backup electrical power to the AFCS.
Provide hydraulic pressure on ground or in flight when an engine-driven pump is not available.
items.explanation: The EHPS can supply hydraulic pressure, for example during ground checks or following loss of an engine-driven pump within its approved limitations.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Hydraulic System – EHPS

items.question: Which components provide DC electrical power in normal operation on the AW139?
options: Two engine-driven DC generators and batteries.
Solar panels on the cabin roof.
items.explanation: Normal DC power is provided by engine-driven DC generators, with batteries used for starting and as backup.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Electrical System – General

items.question: What is the function of the AW139 battery system during a normal engine start?
options: Provide initial electrical power to start at least one engine.
Supply hydraulic power to the flight controls.
items.explanation: Batteries provide initial electrical power for engine start and for essential systems before the generators come online.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Electrical System – Batteries

items.question: Which statement best describes the AC electrical system on the AW139?
options: There is no AC system installed.
AC power is provided by inverters converting DC power to supply selected avionics and systems.
AC power is provided only by an external ground cart.
AC power is used only for cabin lighting.
items.explanation: The aircraft uses inverters to convert DC into AC for specific avionics and systems as described in the electrical system section.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Electrical System – AC Power

items.question: What is the primary purpose of the AW139 engine oil system?
options: To provide hydraulic pressure to the rotor brake.
To lubricate, cool and clean engine internal components.
To provide fuel to the combustor.
items.explanation: The engine oil system lubricates, cools and helps clean engine components, ensuring reliable operation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Powerplant – Oil System

items.question: Where are ENGINE OIL PRESS and TEMP indications normally displayed in the AW139?
options: On the engine/vehicle system pages of the EDCU/MFD.
items.explanation: Engine parameters are presented on the engine/vehicle pages on the EDCU/MFD displays.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Powerplant – Indications

items.question: Which system is primarily responsible for controlling main rotor speed (NR) in normal flight on the AW139?
options: Manual throttle control via twist grips.
FADEC governing in AUTO with engine power adjustments.
items.explanation: In normal operations, FADEC in AUTO governs engine power to maintain rotor speed within limits.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Powerplant – FADEC Governing

items.question: What is the function of the ENGINE MODE switches on the AW139 overhead panel?
options: Select engine operation mode such as OFF, IDLE and FLIGHT (AUTO/DETENT).
items.explanation: ENGINE MODE switches select engine operating modes (OFF/IDLE/FLIGHT) for each engine as part of normal and emergency procedures.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 2/7 – Engine Controls

items.question: What is the purpose of the ROTOR BRAKE system on the AW139?
options: To control rotor RPM in flight.
To stop or slow the main rotor on ground after shutdown within specified limitations.
To provide emergency power to the generators.
items.explanation: The rotor brake is used on ground to stop or slow the rotor after shutdown, within the limitations stated in the RFM.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 2/7 – Rotor Brake

items.question: Which system provides anti-ice protection for the AW139 engine air intakes?
options: Engine bleed air and associated controls as described in the RFM.
There is no engine intake anti-ice system.
items.explanation: Engine intake anti-ice typically uses bleed air and control valves as described in the powerplant anti-ice system description.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Powerplant – Anti-ice

items.question: What is the primary purpose of the PITOT HEATING system on the AW139?
options: To prevent icing of the main rotor.
To prevent ice formation on pitot probes and ensure reliable airspeed indications.
items.explanation: Pitot heating prevents ice accumulation on pitot probes, ensuring accurate airspeed readings in icing conditions.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Pitot-Static System

items.question: Which indication warns the crew of abnormal differences between left and right engine torques in the AW139?
options: Visual torque split indication and possible CAS messages as described in the engine indication section.
A change in rotor speed only.
items.explanation: Abnormal torque split is highlighted via indications and CAS messages allowing the crew to recognise mismatched engine power output.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Engine Indications

items.question: What is the function of the main fuel shutoff valves (SOVs) in the AW139?
options: To allow the crew to stop fuel supply to each engine in case of fire or other abnormal conditions.
items.explanation: Fuel SOVs permit the crew to shut off fuel to individual engines, for example during an engine fire or shutdown procedure.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fuel System – Shutoff Valves

items.question: Where are the MAIN FUEL SOV controls typically located in the AW139 cockpit?
options: On the overhead panel near the engine controls.
items.explanation: Fuel shutoff valve controls are located on the overhead panel in proximity to the engine control switches.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 2/7 – Fuel Controls

items.question: Which of the following best describes the AW139 bleed air system?
options: It provides pressurised air from the engines for anti-ice, heating and other services.
It supplies hydraulic pressure to the flight controls.
It is used only for landing gear extension.
It has no function in normal operation.
items.explanation: Bleed air from the engines is used for systems such as anti-ice and environmental control.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Bleed Air System

items.question: What is the purpose of the Environmental Control System (ECS) on the AW139?
options: To provide avionics cooling and cabin temperature control.
items.explanation: The ECS regulates cabin and cockpit temperature and can provide avionics cooling as described in the systems section.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Environmental Control System

items.question: What is the function of the OIL COOLER FAN system associated with the MGB on the AW139?
options: To provide forced airflow through the MGB oil cooler, maintaining oil temperature within limits.
items.explanation: The oil cooler fan system moves air through the MGB oil cooler to keep oil temperature within the specified range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission – Oil Cooling

items.question: What is the purpose of the tail rotor gearbox (TRGB) on the AW139?
options: To transmit power from the tail rotor drive shaft to the tail rotor at the correct speed and torque.
To house the main rotor mast.
items.explanation: The TRGB changes speed/torque and direction of drive to the tail rotor.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission – TRGB

items.question: What is indicated by illumination of a TRGB CHIP caution on the AW139?
options: Metal particles detected in tail rotor gearbox oil.
items.explanation: The TRGB CHIP caution indicates metallic particles in the tail rotor gearbox oil.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission – Chip Detectors

items.question: Why is monitoring of transmission oil pressure and temperature important during AW139 operation?
options: Because abnormal values may indicate impending gearbox failure requiring timely crew action.
Because they directly control cabin pressure.
Because they only affect passenger comfort.
items.explanation: Abnormal transmission oil pressure/temperature can indicate serious gearbox problems that may require power reduction or landing.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission – Indications

items.question: What is the main function of the AFCS (Automatic Flight Control System) on the AW139?
options: To assist the pilot in stabilisation and guidance of the helicopter in pitch, roll, yaw and collective axes.
items.explanation: The AFCS provides automatic stabilisation and guidance, reducing pilot workload in all three attitude axes and collective.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – AFCS – General

items.question: What is the primary role of the Standby Instruments on the AW139?
options: Provide essential attitude, airspeed and altitude information in case of primary display failure.
items.explanation: Standby instruments serve as backup sources of essential flight information if the primary displays fail.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Instruments

items.question: What is the purpose of the main rotor brake interlock logic on the AW139?
options: To allow brake application at any rotor speed.
To ensure the brake can only be applied within specified rotor speed and engine conditions.
To automatically set the parking brake.
items.explanation: Interlocks protect against brake application outside the permitted rotor speed and engine conditions to avoid damage.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 2/7 – Rotor Brake

items.question: Which system provides warning and caution messages to the crew on the AW139?
options: The Aircraft Warning and Caution System (AWC/AWG) integrated with the displays.
The landing gear warning horn only.
items.explanation: The AW139 uses an integrated warning and caution system providing CAS messages and associated alerts.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Warning Systems

items.question: What is one of the functions of the oxygen system (if installed) in the AW139?
options: Provide supplemental oxygen to crew and/or passengers when required by altitude or smoke conditions.
items.explanation: The oxygen system supports crew and passengers when ambient oxygen is insufficient or contaminated.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Oxygen System

items.question: What is the main purpose of the fire detection system installed around the AW139 engines?
options: To detect overtemperature indicative of fire and provide cockpit indication.
To provide cabin smoke indication only.
items.explanation: Fire detectors sense abnormal temperature in engine compartments and trigger cockpit FIRE warnings.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fire Detection

items.question: What is the purpose of the engine fire extinguishing system on the AW139?
options: To allow the crew to discharge extinguishing agent into the affected engine bay.
items.explanation: The extinguishing system allows the crew to discharge agent into an engine bay when a fire is detected.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fire Extinguishing

items.question: Which indication normally accompanies an ENGINE FIRE condition in the AW139?
options: Cockpit FIRE warning lights and associated aural alerts.
Only a change in cabin temperature.
items.explanation: Engine fires generate cockpit FIRE warnings and aural alerts as part of the warning system.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Warning Systems

items.question: What is the function of the AW139 fuel filters installed before the engines?
options: To remove contaminants from the fuel before it enters the engines.
To add water to the fuel.
items.explanation: Fuel filters protect the engines by removing particulates and contamination from the fuel.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Fuel System – Filters

items.question: What is the primary function of the AW139 main rotor system?
options: Produce lift and control the helicopter in pitch and roll.
items.explanation: The main rotor generates lift and provides control in pitch and roll.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Main Rotor System

items.question: What is the main function of the tail rotor on the AW139?
options: Counteract main rotor torque and provide yaw control.
items.explanation: The tail rotor counteracts main rotor torque and provides directional (yaw) control.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Tail Rotor System

items.question: What is a characteristic of the AW139 main rotor blade construction?
options: Composite blades designed for strength and damage tolerance.
items.explanation: The AW139 uses composite main rotor blades for strength and damage tolerance.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Main Rotor

items.question: What information does the NR indicator provide to the AW139 crew?
options: Main rotor rotational speed as a percentage of nominal.
items.explanation: NR indicates main rotor speed as a percentage of the nominal value.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Indications

items.question: What is the purpose of monitoring NG/NP (gas generator and power turbine speed) on the AW139?
options: To verify engine operating range and detect abnormal speed conditions.
items.explanation: NG and NP monitoring helps confirm that engines are operating within proper speed ranges and that no overspeed or underspeed exists.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Engine Indications

items.question: Which system provides cabin and cockpit lighting control in the AW139?
options: The electrical system with dedicated lighting control panels and dimmers.
items.explanation: Cabin and cockpit lighting are part of the electrical system, controlled via dedicated panels and dimmers.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Lighting

items.question: What is the function of the standby battery (if installed) on the AW139?
options: Provide backup power to selected essential instruments and systems in case of main electrical failure.
items.explanation: A standby battery can supply essential loads if main electrical power is lost.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Electrical – Standby Power

items.question: What is one of the purposes of the landing gear warning system on the AW139?
options: To prevent cabin door opening in flight.
To alert the crew if landing gear is not down and locked under specified flight conditions.
To warn of high rotor RPM only.
items.explanation: The landing gear warning system alerts the crew to unsafe gear configuration relative to flight conditions.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Landing Gear – Warning System

items.question: Which subsystem on the AW139 typically actuates the retractable landing gear?
options: Hydraulic actuators controlled by the landing gear handle.
items.explanation: The landing gear is normally operated by hydraulic actuators controlled from the cockpit.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Landing Gear – Operation

items.question: What is the primary function of the parking brake on the AW139?
options: To hold the helicopter stationary on the ground when parked or during engine start/shutdown.
items.explanation: The parking brake holds the helicopter stationary on ground as described in the normal procedures and systems sections.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 2/7 – Parking Brake

items.question: Why is it important to monitor battery voltage before engine start on the AW139?
options: Low voltage may prevent successful engine start and indicate battery condition issues.
High voltage will make engines start too quickly.
Voltage has no impact on start capability.
To set the correct rotor RPM.
items.explanation: Battery voltage must be within specified limits to ensure successful engine start and protect electrical equipment.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 2 – Normal Procedures – Engine Start

items.question: What is the significance of a MAIN BATT HOT caution on the AW139?
options: It indicates battery over-temperature which may require load reduction or disconnection according to the checklist.
It indicates high engine oil pressure.
items.explanation: Battery over-temperature cautions require crew action in accordance with the electrical emergency procedures.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3 – Electrical System Abnormal

items.question: Which system is primarily responsible for indicating airspeed, altitude and vertical speed on the AW139?
options: Pitot-static system connected to air data and display units.
items.explanation: The pitot-static system feeds air data which is processed and displayed to provide IAS, altitude and vertical speed.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Pitot-Static and Air Data

items.question: What is the main purpose of the standby attitude indicator in the AW139?
options: To provide attitude information in case of primary attitude display failure.
items.explanation: The standby attitude indicator serves as a backup for primary attitude information.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Standby Instruments

items.question: What is one reason for monitoring transmission chip and oil indications carefully during AW139 operation?
options: They can provide early warning of mechanical problems, allowing precautionary actions before failure.
They are used solely for maintenance scheduling and not for in-flight decisions.
items.explanation: Chip and oil indications are key early-warning tools for gearbox health and may drive precautionary actions or landings.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 7 – Transmission Monitoring
